ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A conforming or pat phrase: an answer that fits a ready verbal pattern.
EvidenceBody: Frozen-corpus concordance: 143 exact hits in 96 storage files representing 93 independent works. Its defining proverb says, ‘One conforming phrase ties up a donkey for ten thousand ages.’ Yuanwu Keqin uses the label as an immediate verdict on an answer and warns, ‘Take care against conforming phrases.’ Yunwai Ze lists stock replies—including ‘when the sky is clear the sun comes out’ and ‘when it rains the ground is wet’—as dead sayings delivered as conforming phrases; elsewhere he describes people using such phrases when questioned. Yuanwu says his own teaching seat does not make conforming phrases or look-alike phrases. Later commentary can dispute the verdict: Yushan Shangsi says that treating Yunmen Wenyan’s ‘the body exposed in the golden wind’ as a conforming phrase fails to recognize it.
